title: An HI-absorption-selected Cold Rotating Disk Galaxy at z ≈ 2.193
question: Is the CO(3-2) emitting galaxy DLA-B1228g, associated with the z~2.1929 high-metallicity DLA towards PKS B1228-113, a cold rotating disk or a merger, and what are its kinematics and dynamical mass?

recipe.method: ALMA pipeline calibration in CASA, manual flagging, then three phase-only and one amplitude-and-phase self-calibration rounds on the QSO continuum
key_parameters: Self-cal continuum imaging with Briggs weighting, robust = -0.5
assumptions: The bright mm QSO PKS B1228-113 in the field allows self-calibration of the target field

recipe.goal: Make continuum-subtracted CO(3-2) cubes and choose the final cube
recipe.method: Apply self-cal gains to the full-resolution CO visibilities, subtract continuum, and make tclean cubes at several velocity resolutions and robust values; pick robust +1 at 35 km/s for modelling
key_parameters: Clean threshold 0.5 sigma (per-channel RMS); square mask ~2.5'' x 2.5''

recipe.goal: Measure integrated CO(3-2) flux and size
recipe.method: Single-component 2-D Gaussian fit with imfit to the velocity-integrated image
key_parameters: Velocity range -350 to +525 km/s for the integrated image

recipe.goal: Derive velocity field and position-velocity slice
recipe.method: Fit a Gaussian to the spectrum at each pixel with qubefit and use the mean as velocity; blank below 3 sigma integrated flux; take a PV slice along the major axis from the kinematic model

recipe.goal: Fit a rotating thin-disk kinematic model
recipe.method: Bayesian MCMC fit with qubefit of an infinitesimally thin exponential disk with constant rotation velocity and dispersion, convolved with the synthesized beam and compared to the cube
key_parameters: Nine free parameters: centre coordinates, redshift, inclination, PA, v_rot, sigma_v, scale length r_d, peak intensity I_0
assumptions: Exponential intensity profile I(r) = I_0 exp(-r/r_d), infinitesimally thin disk
Rotation velocity and velocity dispersion constant across the disk

recipe.method: Spherical-mass formula M_dyn = v^2 R / G with v_circ ~ v_rot, evaluated within R = 2 R_e, with R_e = 1.678 r_d
assumptions: Velocity dispersion term neglected: v_circ ~ v_rot = 328 +/- 7 km/s (rotation-dominated)
Spherical mass distribution; may overestimate by ~20% if mass is disk-like

recipe.goal: Measure HST stellar emission and SFR limit
recipe.method: Combine HST WFC3 exposures with AstroDrizzle, align to Gaia DR3 with TweakReg, measure F160W flux in a Kron elliptical aperture, derive an SFR upper limit from the F105W non-detection
key_parameters: F160W emission area 112 pixels (radius 0.2 arcsec); 2 sigma F105W limit AB 26.5
assumptions: Chabrier IMF and local NUV luminosity-SFR relation for the unobscured SFR limit
